issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps/val_interval but code reads max_step and ignores val_interval
issues.detail: Docstring documents max_steps, val_interval, log_interval, deepspeed_config; code reads trainer_args['max_step'] and never consults val_interval or log_interval. Validation actually fires every save_interval. A typo on a required dict key risks KeyError on first launch. Pick one name, use it everywhere, and assert required keys at __init__.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery parses directory names fragile-ly with no atomicity guard
issues.detail: load_checkpoint globs any dir containing 'step_' and sorts by int(name.split('step_')[-1]); a stray name like 'step_100_backup' crashes with ValueError, and a half-written directory from a crashed save is silently resumed. Tighten the predicate (startswith + regex) and write a 'latest' marker on successful save, or verify completeness before loading.

issues.description: Outer training loop has no inner max_step check; overshoots and mishandles boundaries on resume
issues.detail: run() loops while global_step < max_step, but train() unconditionally runs save_interval steps before checking. The final iteration overshoots by up to save_interval-1; if global_step already equals max_step on resume the loop exits without saving final state. State the invariant and enforce it inside train() so validate/save semantics at the max_step boundary are deterministic.

issues.description: valid_*_specifier uses whitespace split on a colon-delimited mini-language with path components
issues.detail: args.valid_*_specifier.split() splits on whitespace, but the documented format is 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' where data_json is a path that can contain spaces. One space yields two bogus specs with no validation. Parse the grammar once at the CLI boundary into a small dataclass list, or switch to repeated --flag / comma-separated convention.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats has confused ownership: mutates input in place, assumes key-set consistency across ranks
issues.detail: Function divides tensors in place (callers then rebuild stats as floats), and computes mean as SUM/world_size with no check that every rank contributed the same keys. A missing key on one rank silently produces wrong means. Make the contract pure (return new dict), and either assert key alignment or all_reduce a presence mask.

issues.description: get_global_grad_norm() can return None and is logged unconditionally to wandb
issues.detail: On skipped DeepSpeed steps or fp16 overflow, get_global_grad_norm() returns None, which either errors in wandb or pollutes the metric. Guard it (default to float('nan')) and apply the same care to get_lr()[0] when no param groups exist.

synthesis.summary: Panel verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Three independent reviewers converged on the same core problems: trainer_args is an untyped dict whose documented keys (max_steps, val_interval) disagree with the code (max_step, save_interval-driven validation), and checkpoint resume parses directory names fragilely with no atomicity guard against half-written saves. The training loop has no stated invariant and mishandles the max_step boundary. Secondary smells — whitespace-split on path-bearing specifiers, in-place mutation in _all_reduce_stats with unchecked cross-rank key consistency — all point to the same root cause: data shapes and algorithm contracts have drifted from their documentation. Fix the keys, harden checkpoint discovery, make the loop boundary explicit, and convert the dict-as-API into a typed record.
